stemMd: A vineyard’s early-harvest plots suffered less fungal damage than late-harvest plots. The owner concludes that harvesting earlier would have reduced damage in every plot. Which fact most weakens this conclusion?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The early-harvest plots contained a variety bred for fungal resistance, unlike the late-harvest plots.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The owner records harvest dates accurately.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Some fungal damage can affect grape quality.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The vineyard sells several types of wine.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Early harvesting requires workers sooner in the season.

explanationMd: Resistance is a competing explanation associated with harvest timing. Changing timing in a susceptible variety need not reproduce the resistant plots’ result.

distractorRationale.c: This establishes importance, not the cause of the difference.
distractorRationale.b: Accurate timing does not remove the variety difference.
distractorRationale.e: Scheduling cost does not address the claimed damage effect.
distractorRationale.d: Product variety alone does not explain plot-level damage.
